To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kinematic patterns of quadruped robot locomotion are more complex on ground than in air, and that this complexity is similar to those observed in level ground locomotion of legged animals.
the kinematics of a quadrupod robot with compliant, passive legs is more complex than the motor patterns, but less complex than the kinematics of legged animals.

1) kinematic patterns of a quadrupeds on-ground locomotion can be explained by a low number of motion primitives, and 2) the complexity of kinematics increases with ground contact, through ground contact dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of body compliance and body dynamics in the kinematic complexity of legged locomotion.
the role of body and leg dynamics for the complexity of kinematics in a quadrupod with compliant legs.
the question of whether a low complexity of motor control and a low complexity of leg kinematics can be achieved simultaneously.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the complexity of the locomotion control system of a quadrupedic robot with compliant legs is determined by the complexity of the motor control and the dynamics of the legged hardware, and is not determined by the complexity or dynamics of the environment.
the complexity of the locomotion controller is the lowest possible, and that body dynamics are the main source of complexity in legged locomotion.
a very low number of motion primitives can account for the complexity of the kinematics of level-ground locomotion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinematic complexity of quadruped locomotion is not only dependent on the complexity of the motor control, but also on the dynamics of the body.
the complexity of the kinematic leg patterns of a compliant legged quadruped robot is increased by ground interaction.
we have demonstrated a low complexity, modular, feed-forward controller for a quadruped with compliant legs, which is capable of generating self-stable and robust on-ground locomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of body and limb dynamics in the emergence of kinematic complexity is not limited to the complexity of control, but also affects the complexity of the observed kinematics.
the kinematic complexity of legged locomotion is determined by both the complexity of the control and the complexity of the mechanical interaction with the environment.
the complexity of kinematics is determined by a complex interaction between the kinematic primitives, the mechanical properties of the leg, and the dynamics of the body.
